 Brian Kelly has previously been the head coach at LSU, Notre Dame, Cincinnati, Central Michigan and Grand Valley State. Justin Ford / Getty Imagse 
 By Chris Vannini , Ralph D. Russo and Bruce Feldman Nov. 14, 2026 Updated 2:30 pm EST Share article 105 Former LSU and Notre Dame head coach Brian Kelly spoke with Maryland officials this week about their head coaching job, according to multiple people briefed on the process. Those sources spoke on the condition of anonymity to describe private deliberations.
 Maryland is replacing former coach Mike Locksley, who was fired on Oct. 21 . On3 first reported that Kelly interviewed for the opening.
 Advertisement
 Kelly is currently a game analyst for CBS Sports Network in his first year not in a head coaching role since 1990. He went 34-14 at LSU and was fired after a 5-3 start last season. That came after 12 years leading Notre Dame.
 While Kelly is owed a buyout totaling around $54 million from LSU for his firing last year, that’s paid out over several years and would be offset by whatever Kelly makes from his next coaching job. Kelly is also required to seek coaching opportunities and attempt to offset that buyout, per his LSU contract.
 What You Should Read Next 
 How good is Maryland’s football coaching job? Sizing up the season’s first vacancy
 Maryland's decade-plus in the Big Ten has brought very little football success, and the next coach will have to battle fanbase skepticism.
 “From a conference standpoint, the Big Ten has obviously proved itself to have that kind of appeal with Maryland,” Kelly said on SiriusXM radio last month. “It is a fertile recruiting area, there’s no doubt. That DMV area is a really good recruiting area. I think that they’ve done great things in terms of upgrading facilities.”
 Other candidates for the Maryland job, according to people familiar with the process, include Memphis head coach Charles Huff and Houston head coach Willie Fritz, among others.
 Maryland had a 3-6 record entering Saturday’s game against Wisconsin.
